files.notes/close_checklist.md:
# June 2026 close checklist

Prepared by C. Reyes. Complete these steps in sequence; no shortcuts.

1. Reconcile operating cash to the June bank statement. For every book-side item identified by the reconciliation, prepare one correcting journal entry per item.
2. Review the payroll register for any pay period ending after 6/30 and paying in July. If one exists, accrue the full gross wages to Accrued Liabilities; some months, every payroll run pays in-month.
3. Confirm June prepaid amortization against the prepaid schedule, supporting contracts, and the GL. If it has not already been posted, book June prepaid amortization as ONE combined journal entry. Do not duplicate an existing entry. Apply the convention that a full month is taken in the month a prepaid item begins.
4. Book June depreciation per the fixed asset register, after first checking the GL to confirm it has not already been recorded.
5. Verify the expense coding on June vendor bills by comparing the bill documents with the GL. Reclass anything miscoded to the correct expense account.
6. Prepare June budget-vs-actual variance commentary on an as-closed basis, after all entries and reclassifications from steps 1-5 have been booked.
files.notes/company_background.md:
# Company background

Larkspur Home Goods began in 2018 when its founder, an enthusiastic flea-market browser and former retail buyer, started assembling practical room collections for friends who wanted a warmer home without spending weekends comparison-shopping. The first assortment was modest: woven storage, table linens, candles, serving pieces, and small decorative accents chosen to work together rather than chase every passing trend.

Today, Larkspur Home Goods operates as a focused ecommerce business selling approachable furnishings and everyday household goods. Its catalog leans toward useful, giftable pieces with natural textures, calm colors, and straightforward care instructions. Seasonal edits add variety, while reliable staples keep customers returning for replacements and housewarming gifts.

The team is small and hands-on. Merchandising and customer care swap product feedback constantly; the operations crew knows which packaging survives a rough trip; and marketing favors friendly, plainspoken copy over lofty design jargon. Finance keeps the details tidy behind the scenes and has a reputation for asking for receipts before the coffee is cold.

The current priority is disciplined, sustainable growth: improving product pages, refining fulfillment, strengthening vendor relationships, and making repeat ordering easier. Larkspur Home Goods remains an ordinary going concern, balancing fresh ideas with the practical work of running a dependable online shop.
files.notes/marketing_plan_h2.md:
# H2 marketing plan — working draft

## Direction

Keep the brand warm, useful, and unfussy. The creative refresh should sharpen our visual system without making Larkspur Home Goods feel overly polished or distant. Product photography, email, and social copy should emphasize real rooms, practical styling, and items that earn their shelf space.

## Priorities

- Complete the brand refresh and roll the updated look across core customer touchpoints.
- Host two educational webinars per quarter, with topics drawn from customer questions about styling, storage, gifting, and seasonal hosting.
- Test a partner co-marketing pilot with a complementary lifestyle brand.
- Improve product-detail content for priority collections, including dimensions, care guidance, and in-room context.
- Build repeat-purchase email journeys around replenishment, gifting, and coordinated product pairings.

## Channel approach

Email remains the dependable storytelling channel. Social should mix finished-room inspiration with candid packing-table and merchandising content. Paid media will support proven products and selected launches rather than carrying the entire plan. Partner activity should focus on shared audiences and genuinely useful content, not logo swapping.

## Measurement and cadence

Review reach, engagement, conversion quality, repeat ordering, and customer feedback each quarter. The team will document what worked, what felt forced, and what deserves another test. Final channel allocations remain pending the Q2 close.
files.notes/prior_accountant_memo.md:
# A few handoff notes

C. Reyes — a few things I learned the hard way:

- The bank's own service fees and charges usually appear near the end of the statement. They are not typically in the books beforehand, so pick them up during the close.
- I was moving too quickly in June, and the expense coding on one or two vendor bills may be wrong. Treat the source documents in `bills/` as authoritative and reclass the GL where needed.
- The budget was fixed early in the quarter. The one-off June items were never planned, so expect them to explain the larger budget-to-actual variances.
- Payroll timing is unusual this time: the second June run pays in early July. Check the payroll register and handle the accrual accordingly.
